question_part_answerable: partly: the file cannot measure risk per mile driven because it contains no vehicle-miles-traveled exposure; it can show yearly counts of motorists killed in reported crashes.
metric: Annual number of motorists killed in police-reported NYC crashes
population: Motorists recorded as killed in police-reported motor-vehicle crashes in NYC, assigned to the crash year
filters: Crash dates in 2013–2025 inclusive; valid, nonmissing motorist-killed counts; exclude rows without a usable crash year or with an impossible negative count
initial_data_check: Scoped checks in check_1.csv: 2,132,218 crashes have dates in 2013–2025; each year has rows spanning Jan 1 through Dec 31, including 2025. No missing crash dates, missing motorist-killed values, or negative motorist-killed values were found. The count is zero for most crash rows in each year; those are legitimate zero-fatality observations rather than missing/default values.
data_check_decisions: Keep the full eligible date range and all rows, including zero motorist-death values; exclude no rows. Missing-year rows cannot be assigned to the requested time trend, but the check found none. No changes to the initial plan.

final_plan.question_part_answerable: Partly. The file cannot measure risk per mile driven because it contains no vehicle-miles-traveled exposure. It can show the annual count of motorists recorded killed in reported crashes.
final_plan.metric: Annual number of motorists killed in police-reported NYC crashes
final_plan.population: Motorists recorded as killed in police-reported motor-vehicle crashes in NYC, assigned to the crash year
final_plan.filters: Crash dates in 2013–2025 inclusive; retain all nonnegative motorist-killed counts, including zero; no rows are dropped by the checks
final_plan.years: 2013–2025 inclusive; observed dates span Jan 1 to Dec 31 in every year
final_plan.limitations: This is a count of recorded deaths, not a per-mile risk: the file has no mileage or other travel-exposure denominator. Counts may change with driving exposure and reporting as well as underlying risk.
